text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
-- The draft budget law, to be discussed by the government today, shows that next year spending will grow most on education and agriculture.
-- Ex-president Lech Walesa has appealed against the Gdansk tax office's decision requiring him to pay almost 350,000 zlotys in back taxes.
-- The national broadcasting council (KRRiT) will probably decide today to whom it will award concessions for the central and northern television networks.
-- Six of the 15 National Investment Funds (NFI) are today due to swap minority holdings of shares in firms involved in the mass privatisation programme.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

-- An OBOP poll suggests that the number of viewers who believe in the objectivy of Polish public television has fallen since last year, although more than half still think it is politically neutral. More people now think programmes favour the leftist government and president.
-- The Independent Centre for Economic Research (NOBE) predicts that GDP will grow this year by 5.1 percent.

-- The period for exclusive negotiations by Franco-Polish consortium Hachette-Wydawcy Prasy on privatisation of news-stand chain Ruch SA expires tomorrow. This means the consortium will then begin talks on a social package.
-- Polish airline PLL LOT reached a net profit of about $15 million in the first eight months of this year, compared with $2 million in the whole of 1995.
NOWA EUROPA
-- Justice Minister Leszek Kubicki threatened to quit if more funds were not allocated to his ministry in next year's budget.
-- Impexmetal SA has become a strategic investor of metallurgical firm Odlewnia Zeliwa Ciaglego in Drawski Mlyn, a company from NFI 13's portfolio, after taking 77.7 percent of its series B shares.
-- The first firm being proposed by NFI 1 for listing on the Warsaw Stock Exchange is Huta Ferrum SA.
PARKIET

-- The National Bank of Canada, Coopers & Lybrand and Bank Pomorski signed a letter of intent for the creation of a Canadian-Polish Entrepreneurs' Fund. The Canadians plan to invest 30 million Canadian dollars over five years.
-- Poultry producer Drosed SA adjusted its net profit forecast for this year to 5.8 million zlotys, a 23 percent increase over its earlier predictions.
-- In a closed issue of speaker-maker Tonsil SA's series C shares, the purchasers of 500,000 shares will be the State Treasury, Krzysztof Niezgoda and Tohoku Pioneer Electronic Corp.
